summary: Niche Pursuits host Spencer Haws reviews five niche directory websites: HappyCow (vegan restaurants, estimated $10M/yr by Growjo), SoakOregon (Oregon hot springs, ~30k visits/month), Sober Nation (rehab directory, ~$250k/yr across a small network, plus an SEO agency for rehab directories), Care.com (acquired for $500M) and MCP.so (MCP server directory, 3 months old, ~52k visits/month). Revenue figures are mostly estimates from Growjo, SimilarWeb traffic and an ad RPM calculator rather than verified numbers. The key takeaway is that niche directories monetise via display ads and sponsored placements, and that a directory can lead into an adjacent service business. A Hostinger sponsor segment is included.

lessons.lesson: A high share of direct and returning visitors signals a useful reference resource that builds repeat traffic.
Personal experience in a niche gives a trust and content edge (Sober Nation).
Directories can become lead-gen assets or springboards to adjacent services such as an agency.
New technology waves create early directory opportunities; MCP.so reached ~52k visits in three months.
Replicating a proven directory structure across regions or topics (sister state sites) is a low-risk scaling path.
Collecting emails through a gated funnel builds a valuable audience asset.

evidence_quality.rationale: Second-hand listicle with revenue inferred from SimilarWeb, Growjo and RPM assumptions. Only the Sober Nation figure comes from the owner (via an earlier podcast), and it is restated loosely. Transcript is Whisper-tiny with some mis-heard words.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Hostinger sponsor segment with affiliate-style coupon code 'niche'; Niche Pursuits also sells site-building content and tools.
